label: late original-phase positions (t>=6) in long sequences, gated by first token
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (99.7% of mass) at absolute positions t=5..8 (t=6,7 carry ~83% of mass), so it shows up only in sequences with L>=6 and mostly in the last 1-3 original tokens before <DEL>. Never fires at t<=4, never in the copy phase, and only rarely at the delimiter. (phase==0)&(t>=6) covers 93% of activations and 96% of mass, but only ~19% of those steps are active. Which ones fire depends heavily on the sequence content, mainly the first original token: when it is y, e, j, u, n or g, precision rises to 0.33-0.59 (y is highest, and y is the first token in most of the top examples), while first tokens like o, l, m, x, 3 almost never fire. The second token also shifts the rate (e.g. orig(1)=a or y gives about 0.57 vs about 0.40). No single token being present or absent in the prefix explains it. The content dependence looks distributed, so the predicate only captures part of it. The top activations come at t=6-7 in sequences starting with y.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: i, m, r, h, 3, o; least: n, c, w, q) and the first original token (most: y, e, u, n, j, g; least: p, l, 3, o); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=7, L=9 & t=7.
